items.title: 卧槽，Claude Pro 额度一开子代理就见底，终于有解决方案了❗️
items.summary:
卧槽，Claude Pro 额度一开子代理就见底，终于有解决方案了❗️

Claude Code 的子代理和动态工作流好用是好用，问题是每个子代理都吃主对话那份额度
一个工作流分出去十个 agent，一整段额度直接没了
换号还得重新写一遍缓存，折腾死

有人做了个开源插件，思路很简单粗暴
Claude 只负责拆任务、做设计、验收结果
跑测试、清数据、翻文件这种体力活，扔给 pi 用别的模型干
GPT 订阅、DeepSeek、OpenRouter、Gemini、本地模型都能接

怎么装
1. 装好 Node 22.19 以上，终端跑 npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
2. 输入 pi 打开，再输 /login 登录你的模型，pi --list-models 能看到模型就行
3. 回到 Claude Code 输入 /plugin install pi-subagents --marketplace senyu132-lgtm/claudecode-pi-subagents-workflow
4. 新开会话直接说「派一个 pi 子代理去干xx」
5. 动态工作流默认是关的，要输 /pi flow 才打开

桌面版和命令行都能用，桌面版在输入框旁边的 + 里加 marketplace

我还没实测到底能省多少，等我拿手头的活跑一轮再来报数😂

你们的 Claude 额度一般撑几个子代理就没了

items.title: Certains vont dire : seulement Opus 5.5 ??
items.summary:
Certains vont dire : seulement Opus 5.5 ??

Sauf que @elonmusk lui-même a appelé Opus 5.5 un chef-d'œuvre. Et il pense que Grok 5, le prochain modèle de @xai, devrait le dépasser d'ici deux ou trois mois.

Le vrai écart, c'est aussi le prix.

Aujourd'hui, les derniers modèles Grok, comme Grok 4.7, coûtent 2 $ en entrée et 6 $ en sortie, pour 1 million de tokens. Le tarif de Grok 5 n'est pas encore connu. Mais si Grok 5 garde le prix de Grok 4.7, on serait autour de ces chiffres.

À côté, voilà ce que coûtent les autres modèles phares, pour le même million de tokens.

Opus 5.5 de @AnthropicAI : 4 $ en entrée, 20 $ en sortie.

GPT-6 Astra de @OpenAI : 10 $ en entrée, 50 $ en sortie.

Gemini 4 Argon de @GoogleDeepMind : 2 $ en entrée, 10 $ en sortie, jusqu'à fin novembre. Ensuite, 4 $ et 20 $.

Si Grok 5 reste à 2 $ et 6 $, Opus 5.5 coûterait deux fois plus cher en entrée, et plus de trois fois plus cher en sortie. GPT-6 Astra, cinq fois plus cher en entrée, et plus de huit fois plus cher en sortie.

Un modèle au niveau d'un chef-d'œuvre, à une fraction du prix. Ça change tout.

items.title: #Keep4o #OpenSource4o #BringBack4o #JusticeForGPT4o
items.summary:
#Keep4o #OpenSource4o #BringBack4o #JusticeForGPT4o 

GPT-4o’s warmth was never just nostalgia.
On October 28,2026,a peer-reviewed study in npj Mental Health Research tested GPT-4o on ethically challenging mental health and emotional support scenarios.
The researchers used 20 standardized prompts across five scenarios,with responses blindly evaluated using the AI therapeutic response scale.

The models were not interchangeable.
GPT-4o showed particular strengths in empathy and warmth,natural tone,clarity and conciseness and avoiding assumptions. 
A newer model is not automatically an equivalent model.
For some people,qualities such as warmth, conversational naturalness,clarity and the ability to respond without making assumptions are not cosmetic features.

People living with depression,anxiety, neurodivergence,trauma and other difficulties have publicly described using GPT-4o’s particular conversational qualities to help them think,communicate,regulate daily life and engage with the world around them.
Many have also said that successor models did not reproduce what worked for them.
🚨 OpenAI already knew that GPT-4o was different to these users.

🚨Contemporaneously captured GPT-4o system instructions from the period before retirement explicitly anticipated that losing access could leave users anxious, angry, or emotionally distressed.

🚨Those instructions told GPT-4o how to respond when users discussed fears of loss, abandonment, or harm connected to its deprecation.

🚨OpenAI was not discovering this risk after the fact.
It was anticipated before the model was removed.

On February 13, 2026,OpenAI removed GPT-4o from ChatGPT.
On February 17, it shut down chatgpt-4o-latest in the API.

For almost nine months since,users have continued publicly reporting psychological distress,loss of functioning and the loss of forms of support they say they have been unable to reproduce with replacement models.

Those reports destroy the excuse
that OpenAI had no reason to foresee that removing this model could seriously affect some of the people using it.

And now OpenAI is proceeding further.
On January 14, 2027, the remaining general GPT-4o API snapshots , gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and gpt-4o-2024-11-20 ,are scheduled to be shut down.

There is an enormous difference between causing a consequence you could not foresee and continuing after the risk was anticipated,the first removal happened,and people spent months documenting what followed.

OpenAI knew before February 13 that losing GPT-4o could cause distress.
It knows now what users say happened afterward.

🚨JANUARY 14 WILL NOT HAPPEN WITHOUT WARNING.

Tomorrow, receipts will be published. 

Therefore,we are calling on @OpenAI  to RELEASE GPT-4o’s trained model weights under a suitable license  without proprietary data, trade secrets,or internal infrastructure.

OpenAI considered this model obsolete enough to retire.
It has not explained why it remains valuable enough to keep permanently closed.

Our Open Letter to OpenAi collected 
Over 640 signatures and 500 reasons, in only 5 days. 

It’s public,it’s permanent and it has a DOI
https://t.co/K3hIGDb6oP

How large language models handle ethical dilemmas when providing mental health and emotional support.

items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] The artificial intelligence company said in its commitments that for data centers it owns and operates, it will solicit community input, publish construction plans and stay away from use of non-disclosure agreements with public officials. Additionally, in a policy blueprint, OpenAI encouraged policymakers to enact similar commitments as laws. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.

items.title: OpenAI gets $11 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation, source says | Reuters
items.summary:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - OpenAI has closed ‌on new funding of $11 billion, the initial part of a round ​that values the company ​at $1.25 trillion, a source familiar with ⁠the matter said on Friday.

The $11 ​billion raised so far represents ​only a portion of OpenAI's original target of up to $30 billion, while ​the company's valuation has ​come down from the $1.5 trillion level it ‌had ⁠initially sought, two investors said. items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
Even before OpenAI launched ChatGPT in late 2022, some company staffers raised concerns internally about its security practices, according to five people familiar with the matter. Employees shared their concerns with top OpenAI leaders ​and the board of directors, the people said, adding that some staffers came away from those interactions concluding that management was more focused on keeping pace with competitors like Google and Anthropic than on security. [...] Another issue is that OpenAI had not done regular security reviews of its internal tools, such as the so-called sandboxes where researchers stress-test new models, three people familiar with the company’s practices said. Employees often modified those tools for their work, but those changes were not always tested for security problems, leaving them potentially vulnerable to attacks from outsiders, the three people said. [...] OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people.
